vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ai-persona-os
Version: 1.5.6

This skill bundle is designed with a strong emphasis on security and agent reliability. It includes extensive 'cognitive inoculation' instructions in `SKILL.md`, `SECURITY-template.md`, and `references/security-patterns.md` to protect the AI agent from prompt injection attacks. All file operations are strictly confined to the `~/workspace/` directory, and the use of the `exec` tool is heavily guarded by explicit instructions for mandatory input sanitization, explanation of commands, and user approval. Persistence mechanisms like cron jobs are explicitly opt-in and require manual user action via the `openclaw` CLI. There is no evidence of intentional data exfiltration, unauthorized network activity for core setup, or malicious execution patterns. The skill actively promotes secure practices and self-auditing.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements, files, and runtime instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (an agent-focused workspace/os); nothing requests unrelated credentials or installs, though the agent is explicitly instructed to run shell commands in the user's workspace and you should review/approve those actions.

dimensions.detail: The name/description describe an agent 'OS' that organizes files and runs workspace maintenance; the declared required binaries (bash, sed, find, wc, stat, grep) and the shipped templates/scripts are appropriate for that purpose. No unexpected cloud credentials, network endpoints, or unrelated packages are required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to operate via exec and to perform file creation/reads/writes under ~/workspace only, and to ask the user before initial setup or any opt-in actions (cron/gateway). This stays within the stated scope, but it does grant the agent the ability to run shell commands — so users should verify each exec approval popup before consenting. The skill strongly enforces verbatim outputs and strict flows, which is a design choice rather than a security violation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided and files are instruction/templates only. The only executable artifacts are small shell template scripts intended to be copy-pasted/opt‑in; nothing is automatically downloaded or extracted from external URLs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables or credentials for core setup. Metadata notes DISCORD_TOKEN/SLACK_TOKEN as optional for explicit gateway integration — these are reasonable and optional for those features. No unrelated secrets or many env vars are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent system-wide privileges. It writes/operates only under ~/workspace per its own stateDirs and marks gateway/cron as opt-in. It does recommend setting channel 'requireMention' in gateway config when the user opts into gateway features, but changing gateway config is explicitly opt-in.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent with its goal of bootstrapping and running an AI Persona workspace. Before installing/use: 1) Review the templates (SOUL.md, SECURITY.md, HEARTBEAT, cron scripts) so you know what the agent will create and log under ~/workspace. 2) Pay attention to exec approval prompts — the agent is instructed to run shell commands on your behalf; only approve actions you understand. 3) Do not provide optional tokens (DISCORD_TOKEN/SLACK_TOKEN) unless you want the agent to manage gateway/channel integrations. 4) Cron and gateway changes are explicit opt-ins: the skill's files state they are NOT auto-installed, but double-check any commands before pasting/executing them. 5) Minor note: some templates reference an older skill version number (heartbeat mentions 1.4.1 while package is 1.5.6); this is likely a stale template string and not a security signal, but you may want to confirm version notes. If you need higher assurance, ask the author for a short threat model describing how exec is sandboxed or for a signed release/source repository to verify provenance.
